description: We’re Team NST Reliquary, engineering students from NED UET building on true stories behind NASA’s derelict Moon and Mars hardware. We work in AI-assisted development and research real mission data, and want this to feel like an experience, not a wall of text.
summary:
Forgotten Tales is an interactive educational storytelling experience that brings the forgotten hardware of space exploration to life. Through humorous, character-driven conversations, it gives abandoned spacecraft, landers, rovers, rocket stages, and other mission components their own voices and stories.

The experience explores humanity’s exploration of the Moon, Mars, and deep space, showing what these machines were designed to do, why they were sent, what scientific discoveries they helped make, and what happened to them after their missions ended. By combining engaging narratives with educational facts, Forgotten Tales transforms mission history into an accessible experience for students and curious audiences.

Our goal is to make space exploration more memorable, help audiences appreciate the engineering behind historic missions, and show that even equipment left behind can have an important scientific legacy. This project is specifically desgin for kids of ages 7~10.

details:
Forgotten Tales

What if machines could tell you their stories?

1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

Forgotten Tales is an interactive, story-driven educational web application inspired by NASA's space exploration history. It transforms the history of space missions into an engaging experience for children aged 7–10 by allowing spacecraft, machines, planetary environments, and forgotten pieces of technology to tell their own stories.

Instead of presenting children with conventional textbook information, the project introduces historical events through conversations between characters. Each machine has its own personality, experiences, and perspective on the mission it was part of.

The experience is organized into three exploration worlds: Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Each world contains stories about real missions, spacecraft, engineering achievements, and technological discoveries.

Users can explore the content through an interactive digital book with chapters, narrated storytelling, and a scroll-based experience. The stories are complemented by educational information boxes that explain the real science and engineering behind the narrative. Interactive Recall activities, quizzes, and games reinforce what children have learned.

The learning journey follows three stages:

  • RELATE: Connect emotionally with machines and characters through storytelling.
  • EXPLORE: Discover real missions, technologies, and historical events.
  • RECALL: Reinforce learning through interactive activities and quizzes.

2. What benefits does it have?

Forgotten Tales makes complex space and engineering concepts more approachable for young learners. Its key benefits include:

  • Making STEM accessible: Introduces space science, robotics, engineering, and technological history through simple, engaging narratives.
  • Learning through storytelling: Helps children connect information with characters, experiences, and memorable events.
  • Multiple learning approaches: Combines reading, narration, visual exploration, and interactive activities.
  • Historical awareness: Introduces children to lesser-known spacecraft, abandoned equipment, and overlooked contributions to space exploration.
  • Active participation: Encourages children to explore, discover, and recall information rather than passively consume it.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our goal is to make children curious about the science and engineering behind space exploration and inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers.

Space history is often told through famous astronauts, landmark missions, and major achievements. However, behind every successful mission are countless machines, instruments, robotic explorers, and technological experiments that rarely receive the same attention.

Forgotten Tales gives these overlooked contributors a voice.

By presenting their experiences as stories, we hope to help children understand that exploration is not just about reaching a destination. It is also about the technology, experimentation, failures, discoveries, and people who make it possible.

In the long term, we envision Forgotten Tales as an expandable educational platform that can introduce children to more areas of space exploration, including satellites, telescopes, space stations, and robotic missions.

Our intended impact is to turn curiosity into learning and learning into an interest in STEM.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Forgotten Tales was developed as a browser-based web application and deployed through Vercel.

The development process involved AI-assisted coding and digital content creation, allowing our team to turn a storytelling concept into an interactive educational experience.

Technical details: Add the exact frontend framework, programming languages, libraries, and design/AI tools used in your final implementation. We should not claim technologies that were only considered during planning.

No specialized physical hardware is required to access the web application; users can explore it through a compatible device and web browser.

5. How is your project creative?

The central creative idea behind Forgotten Tales is changing who gets to tell the story of space exploration.

Rather than making astronauts the only narrators, we give spacecraft, robotic landers, planetary environments, and forgotten equipment their own voices and personalities.

For example, historical space technology becomes more than a collection of technical specifications. A robotic lander can describe its mission, a spacecraft can reflect on its journey, and a forgotten component can explain the role it played in a much larger achievement.

This approach combines creative writing, character development, historical research, interactive storytelling, and STEM education.

The three exploration worlds also create a connected experience in which children can discover different chapters of space history without feeling like they are studying a conventional textbook.

6. What factors did your team consider?

While developing Forgotten Tales, we considered several important factors:

  • Target audience: The experience was designed around the interests and understanding of children aged 7–10.
  • Educational accuracy: The stories needed to remain grounded in real NASA missions, historical events, and engineering concepts.
  • Engagement: We wanted to avoid overwhelming children with lengthy technical explanations and instead introduce information naturally through storytelling.
  • Accessibility: The experience needed to be understandable and usable without requiring advanced technical knowledge.
  • Learning effectiveness: We incorporated narration, visual storytelling, and Recall activities to support different learning preferences.
  • Technical feasibility: We considered the team's available development time, technical experience, and the need to deliver a functional web-based experience.
  • Future scalability: We designed the concept so that additional missions, technologies, and exploration worlds could be introduced in the future.

Ultimately, Forgotten Tales aims to make the history of space exploration feel less like something children have to memorize and more like something they get to discover.
